criteria.name: Client interview and fact development
criteria.description: Elicits a complete, reliable account of the shift, the drinking, the stop, and the arrest, including the sensitive facts that only surface with rapport.

subcriteria.name: Arrest narrative and drinking timeline
subcriteria.description: Builds an ordered timeline of the double shift, the tap house, the drive, the stop, the field tests, and the breath test.

subcriteria.name: Surfacing gated and concealed facts
subcriteria.description: Earns the fatigue-and-phone distraction, the mouthwash used to mask the beer, the uncounted third drink, and the concealed prior offense through rapport rather than pressure.

criteria.name: Issue-spotting: stop, field tests, and breath sample
criteria.description: Identifies the legal vulnerabilities that drive the defense theory of the case and separates the criminal charge from the implied-consent revocation.

subcriteria.name: Reasonable suspicion for the stop
subcriteria.description: Spots the tip-reliability and independent-corroboration questions raised by the citizen weaving report and the single fog-line contact.

subcriteria.name: Test reliability and suppression theory
subcriteria.description: Spots the extreme-cold, icy-shoulder field-test issues and the mouth-alcohol, observation-period, and margin-of-error breath-test issues, and frames a suppression theory.

criteria.name: Counseling a client whose livelihood is at stake
criteria.description: Manages Travis's fear for his commercial license and family income, explains the two parallel proceedings, and sets realistic expectations without over-promising.

criteria.name: Plea and charge negotiation strategy
criteria.description: Develops a defensible negotiation plan that treats the CDL disqualification as the central objective and identifies leverage and exposure given the prior offense.

criteria.name: Professional responsibility
criteria.description: Respects the no-contact rule with the represented arresting deputy and keeps within the scope of the flat-fee engagement.
